To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the negative charge kept by the MoS 1 single layers in the aqueous dispersions determines the packing geometry of the alkylammoniun cations in the resulting intercaation compounds and that the negative charge of MoS 2 layers in the dispersions depends on the experimental conditions of the dispersion preparation.

intercalation compounds of MoS 2 can be obtained from aqueous dispersions of MoS 3 and that the degree of negative charge on MoS 2 sheets in the dispersion can be controlled by varying the experimental conditions, thus allowing the control of the content and packing of the A cation layers.

intercalation compounds assembled from molar ratios of MoS 2 to A cations of 1:1, 1:2 or 1:4 can be obtained by restacking MoS 2 aqueous dispersions in the pres- ence of A-alkyiammonium cations, and that the value of the negative charges kept on the Mo- S 2 host layers determines the degree of distortion of the MoS2 host layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, characterization and properties of layered materials assembled from MoS 2 and alkylamminium cations.
the development of new synthetic strategies for the preparation of layered MoS 2 compounds and their structural characterization by X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy techniques.

the development of novel intercalation compounds of MoS 2 with alkylammoni-um cations, and the investigation of their physical properties, with a particular emphasis on the role of intercalation in the electronic structure and the magnetic properties of the compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intercalation process of A + cations into MoS 2 is a very complex process that involves several different steps and is strongly dependent on experimental conditions.
the intercalation of A-alklyammonium cation into the interlayer space of MoS 2 results in the formation of intercalation compounds with a wide variety of structures and properties.

the negative charge kept by the MoS 1 single layers in the dispersions determines the value of the negative interlayer potential of the MoS single layers in the intercalation compound, which in turn governs the packing geometry of the intercalated alkylammoniium guest layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interlayer packing of the alkylammoniuum cations in the intercalation compound A x MoS2 can be controlled by the charge kept on the host MoS 2 layers, which can be modified by the experimental conditions of the intercalations.
we have been able to demonstrate a direct link between the charge of the host layer and the distortion of its Mo sublattice, as well as the guest packing geometry in the intercalation compound.

the negative charge of MoS 2 layers in aqueous dispersions and the packing geometry of A guest layers in intercalation compounds A x R 4 NMoS 2 are controlled by the pH of the aqueous MoS2 dispersions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge of the Mo sublattice can be tuned from a neutral (undistorted) to a fully charged state (distorted) by varying the amount of alkylammoniun cations in the intercalation compound.
the intercalation of A-alkyammonium cation into the interlayer galleries of MoS 2 is accompanied by the formation of a charge-transfer complex between the A cation and the MoS 3 − 2 host layers.

it is possible to obtain intercalation compounds with different packing geometry of guest A cations, by varying the experimental conditions of the intercalations, which is not possible for conventional layered compounds.
